tweets: Śrī Veṅkaṭeśvara of Tirumala — Viṣṇu enshrined atop Veṅkaṭādri, one of the seven hills guarding Āndhra. Purāṇic tradition (Varāha & Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇas) holds this as the one place he chose to abide through the Kali Yuga — a living Vaikuṇṭha on earth.

Above the sanctum rises the gold-clad Ānanda Nilayam vimāna, gilded over centuries by Vijayanagara-era royal patrons. Today the shrine draws tens of thousands of pilgrims daily, among the most visited sites on Earth. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history
